Advocacy Updates from the International Cheese Federation
This archive page from the International Cheese Federation details various advocacy efforts and policy discussions impacting cheese producers. Articles cover federal regulations like preventive controls and raw-milk aging rules, labeling standards for terms like 'aged' and 'raw milk', proposed tariffs on imported cheese, milk pricing reform, and the complexities of interstate cheese sales, often highlighting their impact on small-scale operations.

Four months until the small-producer deadline 

 

Very small operations get until late January to comply with the federal preventive-controls rule, and members who assumed they were exempt outright are finding out otherwise.

What ‘aged’ actually has to mean on the label 

 

Federal standards fix the name on a lot of cheese labels, but words like ‘aged,’ ‘farmstead,’ and ‘raw milk’ aren’t pinned down the same way — and members want that gap closed. 


Continue Reading

Advocacy 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


The 60-day line, and who’s asking to move it 

 

The federal rule letting raw-milk cheese cross state lines only after 60 days of aging hasn’t moved in decades. Members are split on whether it should. 


Continue Reading

Yuri Lee 




 


The paperwork that proves the exemption 

 

Federal food-safety rules exempt many small dairy processors from the full preventive-controls plan, but the exemption isn’t automatic — and members keep asking us to explain how to document it.

The comment window closes Monday 

 

A federal comment period on a proposed tariff list touching most imported cheese closes next Monday, and we want your operational experience in the record.

What we’re asking for on pricing reform

A labeling proposal worth your comment 

 

A proposed change to ingredient and standard-of-identity labeling is open for comment this spring, and it would land differently on a two-person creamery than on a large plant.
